chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The gift (of oneself) is not permissible except for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and as for others, then marriage is not valid except with a dower.

key_terms.الْهِبَةُ: Gift (specifically of oneself in marriage context)

ai.seo_question: What is required for a valid marriage if a woman gifts herself to a man other than the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between the unique status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and other men regarding marriage contracts. While the Prophet could accept a woman's self-gift (hibah) without a formal dower, as seen in the case of Zaynab bint Jahsh, all other men require a specified mahr to validate the nikah. This ruling underscores the general principle that dower is a fundamental pillar of Islamic marriage contracts for the broader community.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, form Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The gifting is not Permissible except for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, and as for others, so a marriage is not correct except with a dower’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

(A woman’s) gifting herself is not lawful except to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and in other people’s case, marriage is not proper without mahr (dower).”’
